title: Qt: add limit + offset options when loading a file.
description:
When loading very large files, it can be very convenient to load just a part of the file (limit) starting at a certain point (offset). This change adds those 2 new options when loading files.

Supports negative offsets as well.

Should `limit` and `offset` be named `frames_limit` and `frames_offset` (or something similar) to explicit tell this is counting frames and not bytes?
I started with packets_limit and packets_offset. Later changed to limit/offset since it sounded redundant to me. I can change them back, btw, if you think it's better.
Personally I think it's easier to read the code when such variables are explicit. We use `offset` a lot in the dissector code.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8789/diffs?diff_id=525954827&start_sha=4a6e0633af78b9989ddabe2fc371a17297808b54#b5b08f5b195975efb2fcf5094f9f4c607bce5365_128_128)
Done
Should it be indicated somewhere in UI that only a subset of packets are loaded?
Good idea. Suggestions on where to put this warning?
`MainStatusBar::showCaptureStatistics()` can be used, maybe also in the Capture File Properties dialog.
I don't know if it's possible to start the packet number column with the offset?
I don't think so. I've never seen a capture starting with it.
done.

"Offset" here appears to mean "ordinal offset in the sequence of packets" rather than "byte offset in the file".  Presumably the UI makes this clear.
I changed the code to use packets_offset and packets_limit everywhere. I changed the UI strings accordingly.
changed the description
@sfdonnelly we discussed about having partial loads and pagination. This doesn't implement both, but it's a start for loading large files without splitting.
